statement: Let n = len(nums). For k with 0 <= k < n, define f^0(k) = k and f^{t+1}(k) = nums[f^t(k)] for every t >= 0. Because the preconditions say nums is a permutation of [0,n-1], for each such k there is a least positive integer L(k) with f^{L(k)}(k) = k. The function returns a result r, and r = max { L(k) | 0 <= k < n }. Equivalently, r is the maximum length of the set s[k] = {nums[k], nums[nums[k]], ...} taken until immediately before the first repeated value occurs; for every k, the number of distinct elements in s[k] is exactly L(k).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 100000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, nums[i] is an integer satisfying 0 <= nums[i] < n. For every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, if nums[i] = nums[j] then i = j.
